C-STABILIZE-SPLIT-GESTURES.Summary: Split View is reachable only through the View menu, Cmd+\ and the command palette, and the divider's double-click spends itself on side swapping. Per the owner's direction of 2026-10-27, double-click becomes the mode's pointer toggle: double-clicking the divider turns split off for the current tab; double-clicking a narrow hit strip at the right border of the editing surface (present only while split is off, about 8 px wide, ew-resize cursor hint on hover) turns it on. Side swapping moves off the plain double-click: it stays on the divider's Enter key (existing) and gains Alt/Option+double-click. The menu item and shortcut keep their semantics.

Goals.R-1: Divider double-click turns split off for the current tab (same state flip as view.split-view; the toggle-off re-anchoring of the remaining pane belongs to C-SPLIT-SCROLL-SYNC R-1 and ships with it — before that change lands, toggle-off keeps today's scroll behavior).
Goals.R-2: Right-edge enable strip: a hit strip along the right border of the editing surface, about 8 px wide, present only while split is off and the container is wide enough for split (800px rule), with an ew-resize cursor hint on hover; double-clicking it turns split on. The strip must not interfere with text selection, clicks or the vertical scrollbar of the editing surface — the plan verifies the layering and hit-testing corners (strip above or beside the scrollbar, not stealing its drags). The strip is hidden in Diff Mode.
Goals.R-3: Swap relocation: side swapping stays on Enter when the divider is focused (existing) and gains Alt/Option+double-click; the swap preference persistence (splitViewSwapped) is unchanged. Arrow-key ratio steps on the divider are unchanged.
Goals.R-4: The View › Split View menu item, Cmd+\ and the per-tab toggle semantics are unchanged; all three entry points flip the same tab.splitView state.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Divider double-click with split on turns it off for the current tab (state, dirty flag and content untouched — the C-29 corner-1 guarantees hold for the new gesture).

Right-edge strip: present only while split is off and the container is wide enough; ew-resize hover hint; double-click turns split on; text selection, scrollbar drags and clicks near the right edge of the surface are not stolen; hidden in Diff Mode.
Swap: Enter on the focused divider and Alt+double-click both swap sides and persist splitViewSwapped; plain double-click never swaps.
Menu, Cmd+\ and command palette keep toggling the same per-tab state; the narrow-collapse rule is unchanged.

Governance: e2e rewritten/added as above; MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY updated in touched files; graph and verification deltas routed in the same bundle as the code; grace lint shows no new errors beyond the recorded pre-existing baseline.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Dragging the right-edge strip to open split at a chosen ratio, or any resize semantics on it — it is a double-click toggle only.
Anything about scroll behavior on toggle (C-SPLIT-SCROLL-SYNC owns anchoring) or pane editability (C-SPLIT-DUAL-EDIT owns it).
Split below the 800px container collapse or in Diff Mode.
Changing the divider's drag mechanics, ratio bounds or persistence.

Constraints.Item: Pointer-only affordance: no new keyboard shortcuts, no menu changes, no new user-facing strings by design (if the plan's UX corner finds the bare gesture undiscoverable and adds a tooltip, it ships as native copy in all ten locales with the locale presence tests — the Discoverability-over-minimalism mandate is respected either way because the menu and shortcut remain).

Existing gates stay green: tests/e2e/split-view.spec.ts 'double-click on the divider swaps sides' is rewritten — dblclick now toggles off, swap is asserted via Enter and Alt+dblclick; every other corner (per-tab state, ratio persistence and clamp, narrow collapse, dark-theme probe) keeps passing.
The working tree carries parallel active changes; the plan runs grace lint --parallel-preflight before any write.
No release or train admission follows from approval; English only in committed artifacts.
